correctness.rationale: At the first step the source Adam-style pre-trust vector is a coordinatewise odd saturation of the isotropic quadratic gradient, so parameter magnitudes and pre-trust magnitudes have the same ordering. A decomposition of any nonincreasing nonnegative vector into prefix indicators proves the sharp cosine bound \(1/\sqrt d\). Expanding the exactly norm-scaled LAMB step then gives the objective ratio and the necessary-and-sufficient universal threshold. The embedded checker independently stress-tests every algebraic component.

value.rationale: Layerwise normalization is LAMB's defining large-batch adaptation mechanism, and later work identifies trust-ratio instability as a practical concern. The theorem isolates a sharp structural limitation that is present even before stochasticity or ill-conditioning enters: coordinatewise Adam normalization can rotate the first update enough that universal descent requires a learning rate of order 1/sqrt(d). The result supplies an exact stress-test boundary for layer dimension and clarifies why magnitude normalization alone does not guarantee objective descent.
